overview.description: Seven Twenty-Seven is an American vying game, often used in dealer's-choice sessions, where players build card totals as close as possible to 7 and 27 while betting between draws.

history.origins: Seven Twenty-Seven is an American non-standard poker-style vying game passed through home and dealer's-choice traditions.
timeline: Late 20th century: Circulates in dealer's-choice and home-game contexts.
1999: Rule descriptions appear on major card-game reference sites.
Present: Still played with table-agreed rule variants on over/under handling and declarations.
history.evolution: The core frame stayed stable, but house rules differ on whether totals above targets can win, bust, or lose tie-breaks.
history.cultural: The game blends poker betting psychology with arithmetic hand-building and variant negotiation before the first deal.

setup.deck: 52 cards. Number cards are face value; J/Q/K are 0.5 each; Ace counts as 1 or 11 (and can be interpreted differently for 7 and 27 in the same hand).
setup.dealing: Each player antes. Standard deal: one face-up and one face-down card to each player. Common variation: two face-down and one face-up initially.

rules.objective: Win one or both pot halves by holding the total nearest to 7 and/or nearest to 27 at showdown.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Ante and deal**: Players ante and receive initial cards. 2. **Betting round**: Poker-style pass/bet/call/raise/fold. 3. **Draw decision**: Surviving players may request one extra card or stand pat. 4. **Repeat**: Each draw cycle is followed by another betting round. 5. **Stop condition**: When no player takes another card, showdown occurs. 6. **Showdown split**: Nearest-to-7 winner takes half pot; nearest-to-27 winner takes half pot; ties split their half.
keyRules: Face cards are 0.5 each under standard rules.
Aces are flexible (1 or 11) and can support both targets in evaluation.
If all but one player folds, remaining player wins without showdown.
House rule on above-target totals must be agreed before play.
A perfect 5-A-A can evaluate to both 7 and 27 simultaneously.

strategy.basic: Track both targets simultaneously; a hand that looks weak for 27 may still be live for 7.
strategy.intermediate: Control pot size with marginal dual-purpose hands and pressure opponents who are likely over-extended on one side.
strategy.advanced: Exploit declared or observed house rules on over-target handling; EV swings heavily between 'nearest wins' and 'over is bust'.
tips: Re-evaluate ace value after every draw and bet decision.
Do not chase one side blindly if your hand blocks you from the other half.
Before session start, lock in exact showdown comparison rules.

list.name: Face-Up Additional Cards
list.description: Requested extra cards are dealt face up instead of face down.
list.emptyOverridesReason: This variation only changes whether extra cards are dealt face up; no distinct engine override fields are modeled yet.

list.name: Declared Side
list.description: Players declare 7, 27, or both; declaring both requires sweeping both halves to win anything.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Declaration-side behavior is handled in showdown and betting logic text; structured engine overrides have not been added yet.

list.name: Over Is Bust
list.description: Totals above 7 cannot win the 7 side; totals above 27 cannot win anything and may bust immediately.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Over-is-bust handling is implemented by scoring comparison rules; no separate engine override parameters are wired yet.

difficulty.easy: Plays straightforward totals with limited split-pot awareness.
difficulty.medium: Balances 7-side and 27-side equity and uses sensible betting pressure.
difficulty.hard: Performs rule-specific equity simulation, including split/declare interactions and fold-equity optimization.

considerations: AI must support configurable above-target policies (nearest, under-beats-over, over-is-bust).
Expected value depends on whether side declarations are active.
Pot-odds calculations should include partial-win scenarios (half-pot outcomes).

phases.label: Initial Deal
phases.notes: Default one up and one down to each player.

phases.label: Betting
phases.notes: Standard poker-style betting until equalized or one player remains.

phases.label: Draw Or Stand
phases.notes: If at least one draw happens, repeat betting cycle.

phases.label: Showdown
phases.notes: Resolve nearest totals for both targets.

phases.label: Single Survivor Award
phases.notes: If all others fold or bust, remaining player takes all.

customActions.constraints: Dealer acts in initial_deal phase only.

customActions.description: Request one extra card dealt face down (or face up in some variants).

customActions.constraints: Allowed when it is your turn in draw_decision phase; optional each round.

hero.title: SEVEN TWENTY-SEVEN
hero.subtitle: Split-Target Vying
hero.tagline: Chase two numbers, price the risk.

synthesis.shortDescription: A betting game where each hand can win the 7 side, the 27 side, or both.

prompts.human: In Seven Twenty-Seven, each hand fights for two targets at once. Bet, draw, and decide when to stop. At showdown, half the pot goes to nearest 7 and half to nearest 27, unless one hand owns both sides.
prompts.ai: Game: Seven Twenty-Seven. Flow: ante -> mixed initial deal -> betting -> optional one-card draws -> repeated betting/draw -> showdown split by nearest 7 and nearest 27. Values: J/Q/K=0.5, A=1 or 11, numerals face value. Rule variants affect above-target handling.

scoring.description: Split-pot payout between best 7-side and best 27-side totals among active players at showdown.
scoring.winCondition: Take the whole pot by winning both sides, or half pot by winning one target side.

penalties.Fold: Forfeit claims to current pot after folding.

scoring.splitRules: Pot is split 50/50 between nearest-to-7 and nearest-to-27 winners. If one player wins both, that player takes all. Tied winners split their relevant half.

nullReasons.targetScore: No fixed target score; play by game rules.
